title: Hide settings sections and the Design toggle that Smurf does not support
brief:
Desktop app (React + TypeScript, folder desktop/). The backend (smurf-server) has no AI Tools, Skills or MCP features, and no Design mode.
1. desktop/src/components/SystemPreferencesModal.tsx: the left navigation has buttons that call setView('tools'), setView('skills') and setView('mcp') (labels 'AI Tools', 'Skills Registry', 'MCP Server Hub'). Do not render those three nav buttons. If currentView is 'tools', 'skills' or 'mcp' (e.g. from an old link), render the 'settings' (General) content instead. Keep the other code paths compiling; prefer a small constant like `const HIDDEN_VIEWS = new Set(['tools','skills','mcp'])` over deleting large blocks.
2. desktop/src/components/Header.tsx: there is a Coding / Design toggle (around the t('Design') button). Do not render the Design button; keep Coding as the only (selected) mode. If the toggle becomes a single button, render just a static 'Coding' label in the same style.
Only change these two files.

title: Right panel: workflow steps show the node type and real status
brief:
Desktop app (React + TypeScript, folder desktop/). The right panel's 'Workflow step execution' list (desktop/src/components/RightPanel.tsx, around the t('Workflow step execution') heading) shows each workflow step with a status badge and a small engine label. For Smurf runs it shows the wrong label ('CLUTCH' under every step) and wrong statuses (a step that ran fine is marked FAILED).
The live run state (from useClutchState() / the state RightPanel already receives) now has these Smurf fields, not in the TypeScript type, so read them with a narrow cast: `visited_nodes?: string[]` (workflow node ids the run executed at least once), `active_node_id: string` (current node), `status` ('running' | 'awaiting_human' | 'passed' | 'failed' | 'idle'). Steps come from the workflow as today; each step's id is the workflow node id, and its node type string (e.g. 'senior.plan') is available as the step's agent/description field - inspect how RightPanel builds the list to find it.
1. Create desktop/src/services/stepStatus.ts exporting a pure function `stepStatus(stepId: string, s: { visited_nodes?: string[]; active_node_id?: string; status?: string }): 'completed' | 'running' | 'waiting' | 'pending'` with rules: if stepId === active_node_id: 'waiting' when status is 'awaiting_human', else 'running' when status is 'running', else 'completed'; else 'completed' if visited_nodes includes stepId; else 'pending'. Never return failed (the engine's failures show in the chat, not per node).
2. Create desktop/src/services/stepStatus.test.ts (vitest) covering each rule.
3. In RightPanel.tsx, for the step list: when the state has a visited_nodes array (Smurf run), compute each badge with stepStatus and map to the existing badge styles/labels (completed -> the existing COMPLETED look, running -> the existing running/active look, waiting -> an amber 'WAITING' badge, pending -> the existing pending/idle look); and replace the engine label under each step ('CLUTCH') with the step's node type string (e.g. 'senior.plan'). Keep the old behaviour when visited_nodes is absent. Smallest possible change in RightPanel.tsx.
